Agent Observability SDKs provide automatic instrumentation as well as manual instrumentation APIs to provide observability and insights into your LLM applications.
SDKs are available for Python, Node.js, Java, and Go (experimental).

Used both Datadog and New Relic in large-scale production apps and, given the costs, still not very impressed by the DX/UX.
Two favourite Datadog features: 1) clicking a field and turning it into a custom search dimension with one more click, and 2) flame graphs. "Delicious flame graphs."
"Datadog is cool but the price is ridiculously high for small orgs."
One user called Datadog one of their favorite providers. They said its pricing is great for small businesses but probably unaffordable for larger businesses.
"Datadog's server hexagon map/chart thingie is something else. The kind of innovation that wins prizes."
One user said their Datadog UI experience was "reminiscent of something produced from a dog's rear end... Definitely a product where no one in the org said 'no' to an idea. Felt very Atlassian."

One user likes Datadog but finds it prohibitively expensive for monitoring serverless applications, even with negotiated rates. Their Datadog bill is many orders of magnitude higher than their AWS bill, so they are looking for alternatives.
One commenter called outlier analysis a key advantage of Datadog and New Relic.
"I'm a happy customer for several years."
Used Datadog at a previous job and loved it. "I love how quick they were to add support for new things and how easy it was to configure everything."
One user loves the product, with one annoyance: live tail and log lines show up from the top scrolling down, the opposite of how regular logs scroll.

Custom Metrics usage went unbilled for a long time, then Datadog "soft-launched" billing for it without notice and the monthly bill jumped almost 400%. A refund request was escalated through many layers and was still pending after 20+ days. "Love their product, hate their shady billing."
One user received 9+ sales calls in a month after telling Datadog their org wasn't interested. "It's soured me on them altogether."
Another user says Datadog sales cold-called their private number despite the do-not-call list. At conferences, booth staff kept following and pitching after the user said "not interested."
One user did not renew their contract after the synthetics product price rose 100x from its initial release. "The product is reliable, but billing is troubling."
"Datadog is stupidly expensive for what it provides. Don't recommend."
One commenter said Datadog's APM traces are the one thing that locks companies into Datadog.

One team switched from the Datadog agent to the OpenTelemetry agent. They found Datadog the worst commercial provider at showing those traces: everything is labeled io.opentelemetry.something, making it hard to read. Honeycomb, New Relic and Lightstep were tried for comparison.
"Datadog support is hot garbage, and for the amount of money I've sent them over the years they ignore feature requests and just DGAF about customers. They're very hot on licensing though."
"We just moved away from Datadog because their log storage pricing is too high for us. We moved to BigQuery instead. But the interface kind of sucks."
